title: Sprint-Tiling Launch Orchestrator for Regional Cutovers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an orchestrator pattern and playbook we call 'sprint-tiling' to coordinate feature launches across regions and products so that capacity, canaries, and stakeholder windows are balanced across multiple concurrent launch trains. The orchestrator is a lightweight policy engine + calendar automation that enforces: (1) per-region blackout windows, (2) per-train capacity hedges, (3) sprint-level slot allocation and tiling (no two high-risk launches within the same tile for a given region), and (4) automated notifications and cutover handoffs to oncall and product owners.

Scope: This ticket covers PM-owned strategy, calendar contract definitions, runbook templates, acceptance criteria, and a minimal proof-of-concept scheduler that integrates with the existing Release Calendar service. Engineering will implement APIs and a scheduler adaptor; Console & Runtime leads will validate guardrails and dashboard surfaces. We will not implement full UI in this cycle — POC will use existing calendar + automated Slack reminders.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Sprint-tiling policy document published (Confluence) describing tile sizing rules, priority lanes, and blackout rules.
- POC scheduler can ingest a CSV of candidate launches and emit a conflict-free tiling plan for a single region and two product surfaces (runtime, console).
- Runbook templates produced: pre-flight checklist, canary signal matrix, rollback criteria, and stakeholder contact matrix.
- Capacity simulation report showing predicted GPU-hour variance with tiling vs. naive scheduling for 8-week horizon.
- Two stakeholder review workshops completed (Engineering/SRE, Console owners) with captured feedback and action items.

Success metrics (90-day): 
- Reduction in overlapping high-risk launches in the same region by 75% compared to the previous quarter.
- Mean time-to-decision for launch slot conflicts reduced from 3 business days to 8 hours.
- No production SLA breaches attributable to colliding launches during pilot.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Tight tiling constraints risk delaying smaller but urgent launches; policy needs override lanes (emergency/rescue flows).
- Automation complexity vs. trust: early adoption should prioritize transparency (why the orchestrator scheduled a tile) over opaque optimization.
- Cross-team coordination burden: need clear owners for slot arbitration; initial PM-run arbitration expected.

Rollout plan (high level): 
1) Publish policy and runbook (PM).
2) Build POC scheduler adaptor + CSV ingestion (Eng).
3) Run pilot with two product teams and two regions for 6 weeks.
4) Collect metrics, iterate policy, prepare for wider roll in Q2.

Notes on integration: 
- Will reuse Release Calendar API (read-only) for existing slots and post augmentation via PR to scheduling queue.
- Observability: add a per-tile dashboard showing capacity headroom, canary status, and active overrides.

Deliverables: 
- Confluence: Sprint-Tiling Policies & Runbooks (link below).
- POC scheduler code repo + README.
- Capacity simulation notebook and results.
- Pilot retrospective and decision memo.
